correctness.rationale: For each part-pair cut, direct use of the injective-edge definition shows that disjoint cut edges conflict and incident cut edges do not, giving the factor \(\overline{L(K_{a,b})}\). Every two edges from distinct cuts conflict, by a triangle when incident and by a connector edge when disjoint, so the global conflict graph is the join of these factors. Coloring a factor is exactly partitioning \(K_{a,b}\) into stars; star centers form a vertex cover, giving the lower bound \(\min\{a,b\}\), and all stars on a smaller shore attain it. Minimum vertex covers of a complete bipartite graph give the optimizer count. The standalone verifier independently reconstructs the conflict relation and agrees on all tested profiles. The published value in Proposition 2.7 is directly refuted by \(K_{2,2,2}\), where the theorem gives and direct reasoning forces six colors.

originality.rationale: The closest published statement on the same family is not a covering theorem but a false one: Proposition 2.7 of Bhanupriya C K, Dominic, and Sunitha gives the minimum part size for every complete multipartite graph. The direct graph K_{2,2,2} already contradicts it, while the proof here gives the exact all-parameter replacement and all optimal partitions. The foundational complete-bipartite formula is recovered only as the r=2 endpoint. The 2026 maximum-degree paper gives a general upper bound and does not imply the exact decomposition or count. Focused published-finding corpus and web searches found no later correction or exact equivalent.

value.rationale: The injective chromatic index is an established edge-coloring parameter with active 2026 work on general bounds. Complete multipartite graphs are a canonical dense family, and a published 2023 proposition gives an incorrect exact formula on this family. The final theorem replaces that statement with an exact all-parameter formula, identifies the full conflict graph, classifies every optimum, and gives the smallest symmetric counterexample \(K_{2,2,2}\). Correcting a false published family formula and explaining the structural obstruction is mathematically substantive rather than a routine recomputation.
